validity.recommendation: keep as operating; existence, classification, ownership structure and route are all well documented and non-duplicate
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE CONFIRMED, independent of GEM/wiki, across an 18-year documentary record (2008 announcement through FY2024 SEC filings filed Feb 2025). Kinder Morgan Energy Partners LP and Energy Transfer Partners LP announced the 50/50 joint venture in Oct 2008 (Natural Gas Intelligence, 2008-10-06); FERC granted the CP09-433-000 certificate on 2009-12-17 (NGI, 2009-12-21); the pipeline entered interim service 2010-10-12 and full firm service 2011-01-01 (Kinder Morgan Inc.'s own FY2010 10-K, filed 2011); and it remains an active, revenue-generating asset in both co-owners' most recent (FY2024) 10-Ks. Classification is correct: a FERC-jurisdictional interstate gas TRANSMISSION pipeline (not gathering), confirmed by its own NGA Section 7 certificate docket and its listing among Energy Transfer's and Kinder Morgan's interstate natural-gas pipeline systems. No duplicate found against the other 44 rows on the US-gas roster -- it is a standalone 185-mile mainline, distinct from (though a sibling JV-structure pipeline to) Midcontinent Express Pipeline (P0213, also a 50/50 KMI/Energy Transfer JV -- see cross_row_leads). Owner1 'ETP Legacy' is not a real current entity name -- see the attribution concern below.

validity.recommendation: correct Owner1 from 'ETP Legacy' to 'Energy Transfer' -- ETP Legacy is not a current entity name found in any source
validity.researcher_notes: Per the orchestrator's specific instruction to check how Energy Transfer's interest is actually held today: NO source of any kind (SEC filings, press, the operator's own materials) uses the string 'ETP Legacy' for this or any other asset. 'ETP' historically abbreviated Energy Transfer Partners, L.P., the MLP that co-formed this JV in 2008 and that Kinder Morgan's own 10-Ks name as the 50% co-owner/operator through the 2010s. Energy Transfer Partners, L.P. was absorbed into Energy Transfer LP in a 2018 unit-for-unit merger and no longer exists as a separate reporting entity. Both co-owners' own FY2024 10-Ks (filed Feb 2025) confirm the JV is still 50/50 and refer to the counterparty simply as 'Energy Transfer, Inc.'/'Energy Transfer LP' (current legal names) -- Energy Transfer's own 10-K states 'Fayetteville Express Pipeline is owned by a 50/50 joint venture with Kinder Morgan, Inc.,' and Kinder Morgan's FY2024 10-K lists 'FEP 50% 185 2.00 --' among its own equity-method interests without any 'ETP Legacy' label anywhere in either document. Recommend Owner1='Energy Transfer' (matching GEM's own current-company convention used elsewhere in the tracker), Owner1%=50.00% unchanged.

validity.researcher_notes: Kinder Morgan's FY2010 10-K states: 'KMP's current estimate of total construction costs on the project is slightly less than $1.0 billion (versus the original budget of $1.3 billion).' The sheet's recorded SegmentCost of $1,010,000,000 is slightly ABOVE $1.0 billion, while the 10-K's own phrasing places the actual cost slightly BELOW $1.0 billion -- a real but small (roughly 1%) directional discrepancy, not a rounding match. No source found gives a more precise dollar figure than KMI's qualitative 'slightly less than $1.0 billion' (searched both FY2010 10-Ks, the Item 8 financial-statement notes, and NGI's original $1.3 billion budget announcement, which is the pre-construction ESTIMATE, not the as-built cost). Not proposing a specific replacement number since none is sourceable to that precision; flagging the tension rather than silently keeping or silently changing the figure per Rule 7 (agreeing within rounding is a ref; this is outside rounding in the wrong direction).

validity.recommendation: correct FuelSource from 'Fayetteville Gas Field' to 'Fayetteville Shale'
validity.researcher_notes: Every source found -- the operator's own pipeline safety information sheet, both 2008/2009 Natural Gas Intelligence articles, and Kinder Morgan's 10-Ks -- describes the gas source as 'the Fayetteville Shale' (an unconventional shale-gas play spanning multiple Arkansas counties), never as a discrete 'Fayetteville Gas Field.' 'Gas Field' implies a conventional, bounded reservoir, which is not an accurate description of shale-play production. Recommend 'Fayetteville Shale' to match universal source usage and correct terminology.
